prompt.context: Our client is a large national airline that is currently seeking to reduce costs. The management team has identified vendor consolidation as one potential area for cost savings and has decided to pursue the acquisition of their current in-flight food vendor.
prompt.question: They have hired us to determine: (1) Is this a good idea? (2) How much should the airline pay for the vendor?

clarifying_info.a: The airline operates flights only within the continental USA in 30 large airports.

clarifying_info.q: How is the airline positioned in the market?
clarifying_info.a: They are known as providers of high customer service with prices that are slightly above the industry average for certain routes.

clarifying_info.q: Are there other areas of cost reduction being examined?
clarifying_info.a: Vendor consolidation is the only area that we have been hired to examine.

exhibits.title: Annual Operating Costs at Airline Co.
exhibits.shows: A bar/waterfall chart of annual operating cost categories for Airline Co., with dollar amounts labeled for major buckets.

data.In-Flight Dining and Other: labeled within the chart; total context available from the $250M bucket breakdown

exhibits.title: Competitor Research: Indexed In-flight Vendor Costs
exhibits.shows: A line chart indexing in-flight vendor costs from 2012 to 2016E for Airplane Co and four competitors (indexed to 1.00 in base year), plus CEO quotes from each company about their vendor/service strategy.

CEO quotes.Competitor 2: Our vendor costs have outpaced expectations and we will take substantive actions to bring them in line in the next 3 years.
CEO quotes.Airplane Co: In-flight dining has been and will continue to be a differentiator for us.
CEO quotes.Competitor 3: The customer just wants to get from point A to point B fast and on-time.
CEO quotes.Competitor 4: Exerting greater control on quality of the in-flight experience will be a key focus for us in the next 3 years.

exhibits.title: Airplane Co. Customer Survey
exhibits.shows: A bubble/scatter chart comparing Customer Ranking (importance, scale 1-5) vs. Airplane Co Performance (scale 1-5) across six service attributes.

exhibits.title: Overview of Current Contract with ABC In-flight Services
exhibits.shows: A text slide summarizing the terms and business facts of Airplane Co.'s current in-flight dining vendor contract with ABC In-flight Services.

data.coverage: all in-flight dining services across all aircraft and flights
data.other_airline_revenue_share: ABC currently serves 1 other airline accounting for 50% of its total revenue
data.employees: 3,000 full-time across the same 30 airports as Airplane Co
data.route_efficiency: number of routes expanded by 10% through operating efficiency gains

framework: Understand current cost baseline: what share of total costs is in-flight dining, and is this the largest bucket to address?
Assess industry and competitive dynamics: what are competitors doing with vendor costs and in-flight service?
Evaluate customer impact: do customers value in-flight dining, and could ownership improve the value proposition?
Analyze the current vendor contract: what are the terms and what are projected future costs if nothing changes?
Conduct valuation: estimate DCF value of the vendor, including synergies (headcount reduction, system consolidation) and dis-synergies (loss of competitor contracts)
Assess strategic fit and integration risks: financing, cultural fit, vendor willingness, integration capacity

questions.prompt: What is the current spend for in-flight dining services, and what is the projected spend?
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify in-flight dining as ~20% of the $250M Service and Repair bucket. Then project forward using the fleet expansion (20%) and efficiency gains (10%) starting 2017.

math.setup: In-flight dining = 20% of $250M. Projected spend adds fleet expansion uplift on the $50M base ($50M * 20% = $10M) and efficiency route expansion ($50M * 10% = $5M).

questions.prompt: Which competitors should we be most concerned about, and why?
questions.guidance: Competitor 4 is most comparable: its indexed vendor costs have tracked closely with Airplane Co's, and the CEO quote emphasizes controlling in-flight experience quality. Both face similar vendor cost pressures. Acquiring the vendor could be a differentiator vs. competitors still outsourcing.

questions.prompt: How will existing Airplane Co. customers respond to the potential acquisition?
questions.guidance: Customers rate in-flight food as importance 4/5 but Airplane Co scores only 3/5 on performance there — it is the biggest performance gap vs. customer priority. Acquiring the vendor could improve food quality and close this gap. Service is a key differentiator and food quality may be correlated with service ratings.

questions.prompt: What is the DCF valuation of ABC In-flight Services, excluding synergies?
questions.guidance: Use the vendor contract data to build revenue (Airplane Co + Competitor), apply 10% margin, apply 50% reinvestment rate (so FCF = 50% of profit), and discount with perpetuity at 0% growth and 10% discount rate.

math.setup: Revenue 2016: Airplane Co $50M + Competitor $50M = $100M. Revenue 2017+: $65M + $65M = $130M. Profit = Revenue * 10%. FCF = Profit * 50%. Terminal value = FCF_2017 / 10% (perpetuity, g=0). PV of 2016 FCF discounted at 10%; terminal value also discounted.
steps: Terminal Value (at end of 2017, g=0, r=10%) = $6.50M / 10% = $65M
Total Value (sum, simplified, assuming acquisition at start of 2016) = $5M + $65M = $70M

questions.prompt: What is the value of ABC In-flight Services after accounting for synergies and dis-synergies?
questions.guidance: Post-acquisition, Airplane Co will need to terminate the competitor contract (competitor revenue drops to $0) and can shed associated headcount (50% of costs). Revenue halves but margin holds at 10%, so profit halves. The lost value vs. the pre-synergy case is a dis-synergy. Candidate should calculate the post-synergy value and present total acquisition cost.

math.setup: After acquisition, competitor revenue = $0. Revenue is only Airplane Co portion. Profit margin stays 10%. FCF = 50% of profit. Terminal value recalculated at g=0, r=10%.
steps: Total acquisition cost = Purchase price ($70M) + Dis-synergy ($35M) = $105M
math.answer: Post-synergy vendor value = $35M; Total cost to Airplane Co = ~$105M

brainstorming.prompt: What additional considerations should Airplane Co. evaluate before proceeding with the acquisition?

categories.name: Financing
ideas: Debt vs. equity vs. cash financing for the $70M+ acquisition
Impact on Airplane Co's balance sheet and credit rating

categories.name: Integration Risks
ideas: Capacity to integrate 3,000 new employees across 30 airports
Culture and people fit between airline and food service operations

categories.name: Vendor Willingness
ideas: Is ABC In-flight receptive to an acquisition?
What is the current ownership structure and exit motivation?

categories.name: Competitive Response
ideas: Will Competitor 4 pursue a similar acquisition?
Risk of other airlines losing access to ABC or equivalent vendors
Potential for industry consolidation in in-flight catering

categories.name: Regulatory
ideas: Antitrust review given ABC serves multiple airlines
Labor regulations for integrating unionized food service workers

recommendation: Airplane Co should proceed with the acquisition of ABC In-flight Services.
Current in-flight dining spend is $50M, projected to grow to $65M, and customers rate food quality as high-importance but below-performance — acquisition directly addresses both cost and quality.

At an initial outlay of ~$70M and $35M in dis-synergies (total ~$105M), versus $115M in expected vendor payments over just the next two years, the payback period is approximately 2-3 years, making this financially attractive.
risks: Dis-synergy from losing competitor contracts reduces post-acquisition value to $35M, meaning the airline is paying a premium for strategic control, not pure financial return.
Integration of 3,000 employees across 30 airports is operationally complex and could divert management attention.
If Competitor 4 pursues a competing bid, the purchase price could be driven up.
Vendor may not be willing to sell or may demand a higher price.
next_steps: Confirm vendor's willingness and openness to acquisition discussions.
Conduct detailed due diligence on ABC's financials, employee contracts, and operational processes.
Determine optimal financing structure (debt/equity/cash) given Airplane Co's balance sheet.
Develop integration roadmap covering HR, systems, and logistics across all 30 airports.
Assess whether acquisition of competitor-serving operations can be structured to limit dis-synergy exposure.
